name: Se-Jong
meaning: Named for King Se-Jong, who devised the Korean alphabet in 1443 and was also a notable meteorologist. The diagram represents the king and the 24 movements stand for the 24 letters of the alphabet.
endingPosition: Left foot brought back to a ready posture
diagram: A figure representing the king; the page gives no written layout (points A to H are used in the moves).

movements.footwork: Left foot toward B
Left foot to right, then right foot to A
Lower right foot to D, left foot to F
Left foot to right, right foot to E
Right foot to left
movements.stance: Closed ready stance B facing D

movements.footwork: Jump
movements.technique: High side back-fist strike with left hand, right finger belly to left fist

movements.footwork: Right foot to G
Right foot along line GH
Right foot to H
Right foot to left, left foot to G
Left foot along line GH
Lower left foot to C with a jump
Right foot to F
Right foot behind left, left foot to E
Pull left reverse footsword to right knee
movements.technique: High side block with right outer forearm and low side block with left forearm

movements.footwork: Lower left foot to D
movements.technique: Slow reverse pressing block with right palm

movements.footwork: Pull left instep to hollow of right leg
movements.technique: Right back forearm strikes left palm

movements.footwork: Lower left foot to C, turning clockwise
Right foot to A
Right foot to left, left foot to B

notes: Move 18 'left walking stance facing CE' and 22 stance as written on the page.
Several steps have no stated stance (kicks).
